title: Double Pointers (int **)
concept: A double pointer stores the address of the pointer and accesses the original value through an indirect step.

steps.title: Start main function
steps.explanation:
The main frame is created.

Afterwards we create a chain of references: `a -> p -> pp`.

steps.title: 1. Declare integer variable
steps.explanation:
Prepare the original integer value with `int a = 10;`.

The final destination of the pointer chain is this variable.

steps.title: 2. Single pointer declaration
steps.explanation:
Store the address of `a` in `p` so that it points to `a`.

`p` is a variable that contains location information, not a value.

steps.title: 3. Double pointer declaration
steps.explanation:
Store the address of `p` in `pp` to point the pointer to it.

That is, the two-step chain `pp -> p -> a` is completed.

steps.title: Initial value output
steps.explanation: Create a standard for comparison by printing the value of `a` before change.

steps.title: Change value with double dereference
steps.explanation:
`**pp = 20;` changes the final destination `a` value along the chain.

The intermediate addresses (`p`, `pp` values) remain the same and only the original data is changed.
steps.keyInsight: `**pp` follows the pointer chain to reach the final original data.

steps.title: Check changed values
steps.explanation: If you print again, you can see that `a` has changed to 20.

steps.title: Program exit
steps.explanation:
Exit with `return 0;`.

Bottom line: Double pointers are useful for indirect control of the pointer itself.

quiz.question: int val = 5; int *p = &val; int **pp = &p; When, what is not a way to read the value of val?
quiz.explanation:
&p is not 5 because it is the address of pointer p (the value of pp).
val == *p == **pp.

misconceptions.wrong: Pointers Pointers are a special hardware feature.
misconceptions.correct: It is just a variable that holds the address of a variable that holds an address.
misconceptions.why: From a memory perspective, all pointers are integer variables of the same size (32/64 bits).

keyTakeaway: Double pointer is used when you want to change the value of a pointer variable through 'reference'.
